classification.difficultyReason: Split at the zero of the absolute-value argument, simplify each branch and graph the resulting constants with excluded endpoints.

content.prompt: Simplify this expression $\dfrac{|x-3|}{6-2x}$ and hence sketch $y=\dfrac{|x-3|}{6-2x}$.

answer.short: $$\frac{|x-3|}{6-2x}=\begin{cases}0.5,&x<3,\\-0.5,&x>3.\end{cases}$$ Undefined at $x=3$. The graph has open endpoints at $(3,0.5)$ and $(3,-0.5)$.
answer.worked:
$x=3$ is excluded because $6-2x=0$ there.

For $x<3$, $|x-3|=3-x$:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{|x-3|}{6-2x}&=\frac{3-x}{2(3-x)}\\&=\frac12.\end{aligned}$$
For $x>3$, $|x-3|=x-3$:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{|x-3|}{6-2x}&=\frac{x-3}{-2(x-3)}\\&=-\frac12.\end{aligned}$$
Sketch $y=0.5$ for $x<3$ and $y=-0.5$ for $x>3$, with open endpoints at $x=3$.

spec.description: Two horizontal rays with open endpoints at x=3, black axes without a grid, and dashed endpoint guides.
spec.mathematics: y=0.5 for x<3; y=-0.5 for x>3; undefined at x=3.
